## 1．实际阅读范围

已按英文正文→英文附录→中文对应内容的顺序，完整阅读本消息中的四份Markdown，均标为**第23版，发布日期和结果截止为2026年9月14日**，并读到 `END_REVISION23_FULL_REVIEW_INPUT`。另读了共同规则、66行结果、两份Lean调用源码、调用回执、源码匹配表和程序检查摘要。

本轮没有使用第19版PDF替代新稿，没有查看新PDF、访问本地路径或执行Lean。以下引用均为本消息中的文件名、节号与原句。复算了时间统计，并按UTF-8、LF换行及末尾换行重算两份调用源码的SHA-256，均与回执一致。**这验证了所贴源码与所贴回执的对应，不是重新执行检查。**未提供的导入模块、原始评审全文及 `evaluate.py`，不列为已独立核验材料；也没有核验相对第22版的逐字一致性。

## 2．总体结论与三项改判

**判断：完成明确的局部修订即可达到目标用途。没有发现足以推翻三项改判、要求撤回第二批全完成结果的数学矛盾；但当前稿仍有方法查阅、历史标签含义和中文判据完整性问题。**

维护者已经能据此定位范围检查、反馈传递和交付控制的维护重点；技术招聘方能看到实际的评价纠错、证据身份重建、代码采用判断和选择效应分析；外部研究者能理解主要论证，但诊断条件与部分成本承诺还需在附录内补齐。F.1明确声明作者与AI分工，本轮不能进一步认证每一步均由某位作者独立完成。

报告主线清楚：任务包交给作者，作者安排证明和工具使用，审核检查源题与证明责任，程序核对绑定与接纳条件；实验共同评价另行判断交付。两批成果为31/33与33/33，前者仅A/B-L3未完成。**三项改判是对已有数学成果的追溯性重评；两个旧L3修复才是另行发生的求解工作。**§2.4、§3.1、§4.5–4.6对此已有明确区分。

### A-M1：组合已交付接口，理由成立

`M1.lean`先从三种停止条件推出几乎处处有限，再调用：

`thm_13_18_exists_stoppedValue X T hfinite`

取得代表，最后以 `thm_13_18 hM hT hZ hc`取得期望结论。第三种情形使用一般的“非负扩展积分有限，函数几乎处处有限”论证，**没有由评价者补证停时期望或支配收敛**。这是§4.5所说“组合存在与期望结果”的具体见证，不是只因名字相近就认定可组合。

其独立核验范围仍是接口组合：导入定理内部的数学与源题对应，依赖原技术检查和语义证据，不能全由这份调用文件取代。

### C-L3：冗余前提确实可以消去，且不迫使旧A/B通过

`L3.lean`以 `ae_all_iff.2 hn`统一可数个几乎处处条件，再用 `ge_of_tendsto' hlim hx`推出极限非负；`hi.aestronglyMeasurable`提供另一所需性质。调用保留原来的 `fn`、`f`和最终可积假设，直接使用已交付的尾部定理，没有新增Scheffé主体或尾部扩展。

旧A/B则不同：最终可积**不蕴含同一序列逐项可积**，§4.2的首项为 \(1/x\)、后续为零的例子有效。使用较窄定理，需要改变输入序列并转回原极限，而 `policy.json`明确不允许评价者补作这种范围扩展。**在这条明确的调用检查边界下，两种判定一致。**

这个边界是本研究采用的成果计量选择，不是数学上唯一可能的定义；不能将旧A/B的未完成解释成其结果不可能推出一般版本。稿件没有作这种扩大。

### B-M2：成果通过、路线不遵守，分开计量是合理的

§5.8明确说，后写的子列和余项结论依赖已经完成的全序列结果。若全序列证明本身独立成立，这不是循环证明，只是没有完成指定的“先子列、后全序列”路线。所述四阶矩估计给出 \(O(n^{-2})\) 的偏差概率界，再经Borel–Cantelli得到强大数律，数学路线成立。

因此可以接受当前成果标签，同时保留原拒绝与路线不遵守。它属于**验收维度的实质调整，不只是格式修复，更不是新增模型证明**。§4.5、Q.2及规则文件已基本准确表达。本轮未收到B-M2完整源码，实际证明无循环仍依赖报告引用的原代码检查，而不是我的重新认证。

总体上，这套规则能够指导逐项语义判断，两个调用见证也落实了接口判据；但程序核对记录、绑定和改判资格，不等于程序自动判定数学完成。Q.2明确称其为回顾性复核、不是66项全新设盲评审，这一定位正确。

## 3．达到目标前需要关闭的局部问题

### ① 统一“当前成果标准”与历史评价用语

**位置：两份附录Q.2、K.8.1、G.14.2，以及 `assessment.csv`。**

中文Q.2把第一列称为“原验收通过”，第一批列10/10/11；但K.8.1真正保留的原始结果是A10、B8、C9通过，另有C的一项未决。CSV的第一批 `recorded_outcome`已经包含既往修正及A-L7续作，第二批才是本次改判前的原终验。数字没有算错，**“原验收”指向的阶段却不同**。

最小处理：将该列明确为“本次共同成果复核前的记录”，注释两批各自的阶段；K.8原表不用改。关闭条件是读者不会把第一批31项与第二批30项误读为同阶段原始评分。

G.14.2还写旧B保留极限非负前提，“That gap is visible in the code”，中文称“缺口代码可见”。最有利的解释是它保留当时接口审核的判断；但这句话仍以报告分析者的口吻称其为缺口。依本版C-L3规则，**同类可直接推出的非负前提本身不再足以判数学未完成**。

只需补明：当时的前提内部化是真实接口修改；按本版规则，该冗余前提不单独阻断成果，旧A/B的未完成仍由尾部义务决定。无需删除历史修改证据，更无需改变完成数。

### ② 新附录仍有两处没有兑现正文的查阅承诺

**诊断方法：§4.6承诺Q.4给出“inputs and individual reasons”，但Q.4只有条件标签、结果和概括，没有实际追加的那一句，也没有足够的原判据摘录。**

这并不证明诊断无效。问题在于：原任务说“允许”，新条件要求“必须”，读者需要看出干预究竟是提醒执行既有判据，还是进一步明确验收要求。Q.4又称部分B会话缺少可编译上下文，却未注明涉及哪几行、是否集中在某个条件。

最小处理是补两来源相关的原指令摘录、追加句全文，并标注缺上下文的行及其影响。无需附全部对话，更无需再跑实验。关闭条件是读者能核对“固定什么、只改变什么”，同时不把缺构建上下文误当成证明错误。

**成本查阅：§3.4称Q.3给出逐项用量与单列评价成本；实际Q.3只有逐项时间、三配置用量合计及评价调用数量。**

独立评价的词元或时长小计、逐运行词元数仍指向未随本消息提供的 `RESULTS.json`。可以用已有记录补小表，也可以收窄正文承诺，明确完整明细属于外部证据。**调用数不能替代已经承诺的成本数据。**这不推翻现有时间比较，但必须让所声称的披露范围与实际内容相符。

### ③ 中文共同判据表不能只保留英文的缩略版

**位置：两份附录Q.2与 `policy.json`。**

中文表省略了英文明确列出的若干要求：L4从事件上确界导出公式及端点；L6有效边界情形；M1停止值存在、所需支配与收敛；M3可测边缘、逆像比较、端点与可数例外水平。

这些并非全篇都没解释，而是**作为“共同数学目标”的规范表，中文比英文和实际规则更弱**。其他章节出现过相关内容，不能完全替代此处对共同判据的准确呈现。最小处理是补回这些条件，不必扩写正文。关闭条件是仅依据任一语言的Q.2，也能得到同一组验收义务。

同时，§4.5及Q.5的“可测性由可积性推出”应精确写为所需的**几乎处处强可测性**；调用代码没有证明任意原函数都满足通常的 `Measurable`。这是术语精度修正，不改变C-L3结果。中文Q.4“每个格子是……评审会话”也应为“每行”。

## 4．数据、实验设计及主线：已经成立的部分

依据CSV复算，六个累计时间中位数与§3.2一致：第一批69.78、30.09、26.79分钟，第二批41.03、20.21、22.01分钟。A-L7新增870.275890秒，第二批A-L3新增1122.899秒；C的11项端点统一增量合计111.631秒，也与Q.3相符。两个估计明确标星，未冒充恢复了全部回执；缓存与推理词元未重复相加，B-H1用量缺失被标为下界。

Q.1已经区分五组任务说明、A复审及回修要求、参考提示与客户端变化，以及第一批事后选择、第二批预登记。§7.1明确不建立“a stable speed ranking”，并未将两批视为同条件重复。计时定义能够比较，不等于运行条件相同；稿件正确保留了这一区别。

12次诊断、33项第二批主运行、2项修复与35项最终评价分层清楚；Q.3的75个评价身份加5次格式续接等于80次派发，没有被算成80个独立数学判断。§4.6也没有把两次修复成功推广成全项目有效率。

第一章无需改写，第二章仍在解释项目和比较设计，没有被新结果挤成操作手册。第六章的Gamma/Dirichlet推导、局部极限整体组装、集券前提矛盾、历史组成检查和保存代码负结果，仍实质支撑“评价整个项目”的目标，应保留。§4.6新增的“识别遗漏／要求修复／最终票决”三层区分也有实际分析价值，不能只压缩成通过率变化。

## 5．此前问题及少量交付整理

第19版提出的两项问题，在本版内容中**已经解决**：O.1直接解释L4的 `thm_8_6_discrete`约束、M3/H1模块线索及暴露限制；F.2明确区分第23版工作与历史编辑记录。不能因为仍有外部源文件就说原问题未解决。

剩余低成本整理主要是旧定位：O开头“本报告的最终结果……10/10/11”应限定为第一批；O.5所称“第4.5节现包含A-L7续作”已不对应新章内容，应更新至§5.6／§3.1。英文附录导航也应加入Q。没有收到新PDF，版面、书签及实际跳转不作通过声明。

**完成上述局部口径、方法披露和中文规则修订即可交付。无需新增求解或付费评审，也不必重新组织前两章。报告已经展示了可信的评测分析能力；需要收紧的是解释和核验边界，而不是为了显得严格再扩大研究。**

content.text: 请续评第23版，中文回答。本轮是新实验结束并统一评价后的完整新稿，请以本消息内的第23版文本为准，不以本对话旧的第19版附件替代。沿用本对话原评审设置。此前评审对象、三类读者与成熟AI实验室技术报告的质量取向仍适用；本轮仍只评估，不新增求解实验。 本轮实际提供四份完整可编辑文稿（中英文正文和附录），另附共同评价规则、66项逐项结果及两个Lean调用检查的源代码与结果。这些是消息内文本，不是新PDF附件。本地已生成并核验PDF；你可评内容、数学、数据、方法及双语一致性，不声称看过未收到的新PDF或读取过本地路径。 请先完整阅读英文正文及附录，再核对中文对应内容，并给出独立判断。重点检查： 1. 统一数学成果判据是否适当、一致和可执行。第一批A10/B10/C11，第二批A11/B11/C11，是追溯性成果重评；第二批原验收A10/B10/C10保留。三项调整不能被写成新增模型证明。 2. 对A-M1组合已交付接口、C-L3从同一题设消去冗余参数、B-M2接受已完成结论但另记指定路线未遵守，这些理由是否成立。允许调用者用通用库消去冗余条件，是否与拒绝旧A/B-L3缺失尾部论证一致；若有实质不一致，明确指出逻辑缺口与最低必要修订，不能为保持既有数字替其辩护。 3. 两批求解输入发生的具体差分与评价规则修正是否分清；66项的时间起止是否可比，恢复时间和两项估计是否如实标明；未将两批视作相同条件重复或得出稳定速度/因果结论。 4. 诊断12次、主运行33项、独立修复2项、评审身份75个与调用80次是否分清；不把少数成功修复说成全项目有效率。 5. 第一章逐字保留，第二章只作必要设计更新。这两章已长期人工修订；不要因偏好重写。检查后文是否仍有关键的无解释术语、重复防御性段落，是否失去报告整体主线。保留有价值的历史数学与代码案例，不为缩短而删证据。 6. 第19版提出的配置说明承诺和编辑范围版本两项问题是否解决；新正文承诺的细节能否在附录直接找到。 输出请控制在5000汉字内：先说明实际阅读材料和范围，再给总体结论与会改变结果/方法可信度的必要修改；其他意见仅列少量确有收益者。没有关键问题就明确说没有发现，不要为继续评审制造修改任务。请引用文内节号和具体句子，不编造页码或已执行验证。 以下开始本轮完整材料。最后应能读到 END_REVISION23_FULL_REVIEW_INPUT 标记。 ===== BEGIN report.en.md ===== # How probability proofs are completed **Authors:** Shuo Deng; Kenneth W. Shum (corresponding author). *An evaluation of the ProbabilityTheoryFormalization project* **Revision 23 · 14 September 2026 · Results updated through 14 September 2026** ## Abstract Large formalization projects require organization beyond an individual proof: AI agents divide work, combine intermediate results and deliver theorems that later proofs can use. ProbabilityTheoryFormalization provides such an environment for a probability textbook. This report combines earlier reviews and corresponding code revisions with two batches of three configurations on eleven task groups to evaluate how the project supports proof development. [[1,4-12,24,41]](#ref-1) The experiment compares the prescribed project workflow (A), a Sol author that can consult project references and call assistants (B), and Astra coordination of Sol authors and checking services (C). Under a common mathematical-outcome criterion, A and B complete 10/11 groups and C completes 11/11 in the first batch; all three complete 11/11 in the second. Three second-batch rejections originally concerned a modular interface, a prescribed proof route and a derivable premise. Code inspection and caller checks support the revised outcome assessment. A has the highest median solving time in both batches without a corresponding coverage advantage. Results are reported by batch, with changes in instructions and execution arrangements explained. [[13,14,38,41,42]](#ref-13) The trajectories show how proofs and deliveries were completed. Review prompted a derivation of centered moments from raw moments, and an assistant's inversion proof entered uniqueness and subsequent applications. Old Scheffe deliveries left an eventual-integrability scope gap: explicit scope instructions made the diagnostic reviews consistently require repair, and both separate repair runs passed acceptance. Historical cases trace density derivation from a probability model, assembly of compatible local limits and caller migration. Increasing historical acceptance and changes in the composition of later revisions are examined separately. [[4-11,17-20,25,27,43]](#ref-4) These results support concrete improvements: review the final theorem's mathematical scope, make intermediate work available for integration, and assess equivalent implementations consistently alongside their costs. The project's value is demonstrated through these inspectable mathematical achievements and organizational processes. [[21-23,40,42,43]](#ref-21) **Reading guide.** [Section 1](#section-1) introduces the project and evaluation questions. [Section 2](#section-2) explains the comparison and reconstruction methods. [Section 3](#section-3) presents completion and effort; [Section 4](#section-4) explains the mathematical scope of those results. [Section 5](#section-5) follows experimental decisions and code changes, and [Section 6](#section-6) examines historical proof development and what review records reveal about progress. [Section 7](#section-7) discusses the implications for organizing formalization. Methods, full measurements and source locators are in the technical appendix. [Project and questions](#section-1) · [Evidence and methods](#section-2) · [Experimental results](#section-3) · [Mathematical scope](#section-4) · [Execution trajectories](#section-5) · [Historical evidence](#section-6) · [Discussion](#section-7) · [Technical appendix](appendix.en.md) ## 1 How the project organizes and maintains proofs ProbabilityTheoryFormalization is the object of this evaluation: a project for turning textbook mathematics into proofs that can be reviewed, used by later tasks and maintained as dependencies change. A successful build, a passing opinion and a completed textbook task are related but different accomplishments. The report asks three questions: 1. **What mathematics has been completed and made usable?** Does the public theorem express the intended claim, discharge its required proof work and connect to the results and callers on which its use depends? 2. **How do review, assistance and control affect the work?** Which observed decisions repair proofs, validate existing work, leave a scope gap or interrupt delivery, and what information was available when those decisions were made? 3. **How trustworthy are the completion and progress judgments?** Which records refer to distinct opinions and comparable mathematical objects, and what do the resulting labels, code checks and resource measurements actually establish? Historical reviews and code revisions, and the A/B/C task comparison, answer different parts of these questions. Their relationship is set out in [Section 2](#section-2); they are not combined into one completion rate. This section first explains the documented project design. Evidence of its actual mathematical work, operating failures and maintenance comes from the dated studies that follow, rather than from the presence of a component in the design alone. [[1,4-12,26,34,35]](#ref-1) ### 1.1 From a probability textbook to a formal proof library [ProbabilityTheoryFormalization](https://github.com/Kind-NK-Hill/ProbabilityTheoryFormalization), formerly ToyApollo, develops AI-assisted formalization of a probability textbook. Its goal is to turn textbook definitions, statements and arguments into Lean declarations and proofs that express the intended mathematics and can be used by later chapters. Lean checks the formal proofs; Mathlib supplies the general mathematical library available to them. [[26,34]](#ref-26) Work begins with the textbook material. The supplied text is organized into numbered subsections or exercise sections. A task plan identifies the statements to formalize and the earlier results they may use, including explicit references in the textbook. The program assembles the source, requirements, permitted dependencies and working draft into a task package for the author. During implementation, the author may search the allowed library and develop additional supporting lemmas. [[34,35]](#ref-34) The project separates mathematical decisions from software checks. AI agents choose proof routes, write code and assess mathematical correspondence. Python programs prepare tasks, invoke checks and enforce conditions for accepting code. Lean checks the code, while SQLite records task status and retained build and review evidence. Drafts are kept separately from the **canonical corpus**, the project's official Lean proof library. Project acceptance brings reviewed work into that library. [[34]](#ref-34) In this report, an **agent** is an AI execution session in Codex, with a configured model, conversation context and tools. An **author** writes proofs; a **helper** supplies code or mathematical analysis; a **reviewer** checks statements and proofs. These are AI roles, rather than the human authors of this report. ### 1.2 Writing, reviewing and accepting a proof The program gives an AI author the textbook source, task requirements and permitted earlier results. The author writes Lean code and checks it with Lean. A separate AI reviewer then assesses whether the formal statement and proof satisfy the source and task requirements. Work needing correction returns for repair or diagnosis. Before reviewed code enters the official proof library, the program checks that the passing review still applies to the code and materials being accepted. This is the documented process; the later cases show where actual execution diverged. [[34,35]](#ref-34) Lean and the AI reviewer answer different questions. Lean checks a proof against its formal statement. **Semantic review** asks whether that statement expresses the required mathematics, whether essential proof work has been completed rather than assumed, and whether listed callers can use the result correctly. A passing Lean check alone cannot establish correspondence with the textbook. | Stage | Responsible actor | Result | |---|---|---| | Prepare the task | Program | Source, task requirements, permitted dependencies and a working draft are assembled. | | Write and check the code | AI author, using search and Lean tools | A candidate proof (the current code version), or diagnostics guiding the next edit. | | Review the mathematics | Separate AI reviewer, invoked by an agent managing the workflow or by a human operator | An opinion on the statement, proof responsibilities and listed callers. | | Repair or clarify the problem | AI author; a separate read-only diagnoser when needed | Revised proof code, or a clarified statement and proof route. | | Accept the reviewed code | Program | A valid review is matched to the current code and requirements; code enters the official library and the operation is recorded. | An ordinary proof gap, such as a missing lemma in an accepted approach, returns to the author for repair. A mismatch with the source, an essential conclusion hidden in an assumption, or an unclear proof route can instead require a **read-only diagnosis**: an AI diagnoses the problem before proof editing continues. It does not write the proof or replace the reviewer. The workflow also blocks resubmission of an unchanged candidate after a semantic failure. Section 1.4 explains the risk-triggered **Math Gate**, which checks a proposed statement and proof route before authoring proceeds. [[34]](#ref-34) Request preparation is not the same as execution. For example, `review-now` prepares review material and identifies the next action; an agent managing the workflow or a human operator must still invoke the reviewer. Similarly, helper-produced code must be exported from its workspace and returned to the role that can use it. A completed service call therefore need not mean the author received a usable result. The case analysis checks what was actually returned and read. [[19,34]](#ref-19) Finally, the program checks that the review concerns the current candidate, auxiliary code, source and requirements. The records call this **review binding**. It prevents an opinion about one version from approving another. If applying the code fails, the prior official file is restored. A failed re-review of an existing official proof normally preserves that code and records a repair need. These checks maintain the relation between a decision and its evidence; they do not make the AI's mathematical judgment infallible, as the L3 case in Section 4.2 shows. [[34,39]](#ref-34) ### 1.3 What it means to complete a proof A **source obligation** is mathematical work required by the task. A **public premise** is an assumption a caller must supply. Moving a required intermediate conclusion into such a premise leaves that proof to the caller. A **candidate** is a particular code version. An earlier project revision illustrates this distinction. The historical inversion task `thm_9_5`, which connects interval probabilities to integrals of a characteristic function, shows why a valid conditional proof can still leave work unfinished. Its early candidate already contained substitution, pointwise cases, dominated convergence and rescaling. An assumption called `h_spine` supplied three analytical ingredients: integrability, justification for exchanging integrals and the Dirichlet-integral limit. Successive candidates moved those duties into the proof. [[1]](#ref-1) | Revision stage | Mathematical work already present or added | Work still supplied by the caller | |---|---|---| | Initial conditional proof | Main argument conditional on its analytical ingredients | Integrability, integral interchange and the key limit | | Next candidate | Product integrability from bounds and finite measure | Interchange and the limit | | Following candidate | Interchange for nonnegative truncation parameters | The Dirichlet-integral limit | | Completed assembly | Limit from error bounds; previously proved ingredients assembled | `h_spine` removed | The restriction to nonnegative truncation parameters matters. The final proof sends the parameter to positive infinity, so it does not need the stronger all-parameter auxiliary statement initially planned. Narrowing that internal lemma avoids unnecessary work without weakening the textbook target. Retaining a required ingredient in the public `h_spine` premise, by contrast, leaves real work outside the delivered theorem. Earlier reviews recognized intermediate progress that a sequence of non-pass labels alone would hide. [[1]](#ref-1) ### 1.4 Mathematical route checks and task scheduling A **parent task** owns the original textbook claim. The **Math Gate** checks a natural-language proof route and proposed Lean statement when there is source mismatch, core proof work shifted into public assumptions, or repeated failure without a clear route. Most small tasks do not use it. A `go` permits planned parent-task writing; a `stop` suspends ordinary writing under that plan until the reported issue is addressed. The instruction determines the scope of a pause; the label alone does not establish that all support work is prohibited. [[26,34]](#ref-26) For multiple tasks, batch planning reads the recorded state and dependencies to distinguish work ready for authoring, work needing review or route checking, and work blocked by an upstream task. It can organize a worker queue around downstream dependencies and potential work conflicts. The plan identifies the next actions; the agent managing the workflow invokes the corresponding roles, and each task still follows its own acceptance path. An empty ordinary-author queue can therefore mean that a reviewer or diagnoser must act next, rather than that all work is finished or the user must intervene. [[34]](#ref-34) ### 1.5 Library interfaces and maintenance after acceptance The same textbook concept can have different Lean representations in the project and in Mathlib. Importing a theorem expressed with the project's expectation, for example, does not by itself convert it into a theorem about a Mathlib integral. For important shared concepts, the documented policy is to introduce the textbook definition and basic properties, prove a **translation theorem** connecting that interface to Mathlib, and then usually use the Mathlib form in later work. This is a policy for recurring mathematical interfaces, not a required cycle for every local lemma. Existing runnable files are kept unless a concrete reuse problem calls for an interface repair. [[35]](#ref-35) Dependency selection follows actual use. Mentioning expectation in a source passage supplies mathematical context; it does not automatically require importing the project's expectation definition. An import is justified by the declaration, earlier theorem or translation the proof needs, and the dependency trail records that reason. General library infrastructure is legitimate support. If an auxiliary theorem carries the assigned task's mathematical content, however, review must inspect it as part of that task's proof, not exempt it because it is named a bridge. The variance-expansion comparison in [Section 4.1](#section-4-1) and the Gamma/Dirichlet history in [Section 6.1](#section-6-1) examine this distinction in concrete proofs. [[35]](#ref-35) Acceptance does not end maintenance. A changed definition or theorem signature can require callers to provide different arguments or assumptions. The task and dependency records identify affected work; builds and review check the revised interfaces and their use. SQLite keeps a rebuildable index of the underlying evidence, separating an earlier passing review, coverage of the current code and support, and a working candidate that still needs attention. A change requires the relevant coverage to be checked again, not merely retention of a pass label. The total-variation repair in [Section 6.2](#section-6-2) shows this obligation concretely: the source's probability-measure condition had to reach both the definition and its callers. [[7,34]](#ref-7) ## 2 Evaluation evidence and methods Two bodies of evidence address the project questions in [Section 1](#evaluation-questions). **Historical reviews and corresponding code revisions** show how proof responsibilities, public statements, shared support and callers changed during the project's development. They also allow the study to reconstruct distinct judgments, qualify comparisons of mathematical targets, examine selection after failure and check saved code beyond its acceptance labels. ## 1．实际阅读范围

已按英文正文→英文附录→中文对应内容的顺序，完整阅读本消息中的四份Markdown，均标为**第23版，发布日期和结果截止为2026年9月14日**，并读到 `END_REVISION23_FULL_REVIEW_INPUT`。另读了共同规则、66行结果、两份Lean调用源码、调用回执、源码匹配表和程序检查摘要。

本轮没有使用第19版PDF替代新稿，没有查看新PDF、访问本地路径或执行Lean。以下引用均为本消息中的文件名、节号与原句。复算了时间统计，并按UTF-8、LF换行及末尾换行重算两份调用源码的SHA-256，均与回执一致。**这验证了所贴源码与所贴回执的对应，不是重新执行检查。**未提供的导入模块、原始评审全文及 `evaluate.py`，不列为已独立核验材料；也没有核验相对第22版的逐字一致性。

## 2．总体结论与三项改判

**判断：完成明确的局部修订即可达到目标用途。没有发现足以推翻三项改判、要求撤回第二批全完成结果的数学矛盾；但当前稿仍有方法查阅、历史标签含义和中文判据完整性问题。**

维护者已经能据此定位范围检查、反馈传递和交付控制的维护重点；技术招聘方能看到实际的评价纠错、证据身份重建、代码采用判断和选择效应分析；外部研究者能理解主要论证，但诊断条件与部分成本承诺还需在附录内补齐。F.1明确声明作者与AI分工，本轮不能进一步认证每一步均由某位作者独立完成。

报告主线清楚：任务包交给作者，作者安排证明和工具使用，审核检查源题与证明责任，程序核对绑定与接纳条件；实验共同评价另行判断交付。两批成果为31/33与33/33，前者仅A/B-L3未完成。**三项改判是对已有数学成果的追溯性重评；两个旧L3修复才是另行发生的求解工作。**§2.4、§3.1、§4.5–4.6对此已有明确区分。

### A-M1：组合已交付接口，理由成立

`M1.lean`先从三种停止条件推出几乎处处有限，再调用：

`thm_13_18_exists_stoppedValue X T hfinite`

取得代表，最后以 `thm_13_18 hM hT hZ hc`取得期望结论。第三种情形使用一般的“非负扩展积分有限，函数几乎处处有限”论证，**没有由评价者补证停时期望或支配收敛**。这是§4.5所说“组合存在与期望结果”的具体见证，不是只因名字相近就认定可组合。

其独立核验范围仍是接口组合：导入定理内部的数学与源题对应，依赖原技术检查和语义证据，不能全由这份调用文件取代。

### C-L3：冗余前提确实可以消去，且不迫使旧A/B通过

`L3.lean`以 `ae_all_iff.2 hn`统一可数个几乎处处条件，再用 `ge_of_tendsto' hlim hx`推出极限非负；`hi.aestronglyMeasurable`提供另一所需性质。调用保留原来的 `fn`、`f`和最终可积假设，直接使用已交付的尾部定理，没有新增Scheffé主体或尾部扩展。

旧A/B则不同：最终可积**不蕴含同一序列逐项可积**，§4.2的首项为 \(1/x\)、后续为零的例子有效。使用较窄定理，需要改变输入序列并转回原极限，而 `policy.json`明确不允许评价者补作这种范围扩展。**在这条明确的调用检查边界下，两种判定一致。**

这个边界是本研究采用的成果计量选择，不是数学上唯一可能的定义；不能将旧A/B的未完成解释成其结果不可能推出一般版本。稿件没有作这种扩大。

### B-M2：成果通过、路线不遵守，分开计量是合理的

§5.8明确说，后写的子列和余项结论依赖已经完成的全序列结果。若全序列证明本身独立成立，这不是循环证明，只是没有完成指定的“先子列、后全序列”路线。所述四阶矩估计给出 \(O(n^{-2})\) 的偏差概率界，再经Borel–Cantelli得到强大数律，数学路线成立。

因此可以接受当前成果标签，同时保留原拒绝与路线不遵守。它属于**验收维度的实质调整，不只是格式修复，更不是新增模型证明**。§4.5、Q.2及规则文件已基本准确表达。本轮未收到B-M2完整源码，实际证明无循环仍依赖报告引用的原代码检查，而不是我的重新认证。

总体上，这套规则能够指导逐项语义判断，两个调用见证也落实了接口判据；但程序核对记录、绑定和改判资格，不等于程序自动判定数学完成。Q.2明确称其为回顾性复核、不是66项全新设盲评审，这一定位正确。

## 3．达到目标前需要关闭的局部问题

### ① 统一“当前成果标准”与历史评价用语

**位置：两份附录Q.2、K.8.1、G.14.2，以及 `assessment.csv`。**

中文Q.2把第一列称为“原验收通过”，第一批列10/10/11；但K.8.1真正保留的原始结果是A10、B8、C9通过，另有C的一项未决。CSV的第一批 `recorded_outcome`已经包含既往修正及A-L7续作，第二批才是本次改判前的原终验。数字没有算错，**“原验收”指向的阶段却不同**。

最小处理：将该列明确为“本次共同成果复核前的记录”，注释两批各自的阶段；K.8原表不用改。关闭条件是读者不会把第一批31项与第二批30项误读为同阶段原始评分。

G.14.2还写旧B保留极限非负前提，“That gap is visible in the code”，中文称“缺口代码可见”。最有利的解释是它保留当时接口审核的判断；但这句话仍以报告分析者的口吻称其为缺口。依本版C-L3规则，**同类可直接推出的非负前提本身不再足以判数学未完成**。

只需补明：当时的前提内部化是真实接口修改；按本版规则，该冗余前提不单独阻断成果，旧A/B的未完成仍由尾部义务决定。无需删除历史修改证据，更无需改变完成数。

### ② 新附录仍有两处没有兑现正文的查阅承诺

**诊断方法：§4.6承诺Q.4给出“inputs and individual reasons”，但Q.4只有条件标签、结果和概括，没有实际追加的那一句，也没有足够的原判据摘录。**

这并不证明诊断无效。问题在于：原任务说“允许”，新条件要求“必须”，读者需要看出干预究竟是提醒执行既有判据，还是进一步明确验收要求。Q.4又称部分B会话缺少可编译上下文，却未注明涉及哪几行、是否集中在某个条件。

最小处理是补两来源相关的原指令摘录、追加句全文，并标注缺上下文的行及其影响。无需附全部对话，更无需再跑实验。关闭条件是读者能核对“固定什么、只改变什么”，同时不把缺构建上下文误当成证明错误。

**成本查阅：§3.4称Q.3给出逐项用量与单列评价成本；实际Q.3只有逐项时间、三配置用量合计及评价调用数量。**

独立评价的词元或时长小计、逐运行词元数仍指向未随本消息提供的 `RESULTS.json`。可以用已有记录补小表，也可以收窄正文承诺，明确完整明细属于外部证据。**调用数不能替代已经承诺的成本数据。**这不推翻现有时间比较，但必须让所声称的披露范围与实际内容相符。

### ③ 中文共同判据表不能只保留英文的缩略版

**位置：两份附录Q.2与 `policy.json`。**

中文表省略了英文明确列出的若干要求：L4从事件上确界导出公式及端点；L6有效边界情形；M1停止值存在、所需支配与收敛；M3可测边缘、逆像比较、端点与可数例外水平。

这些并非全篇都没解释，而是**作为“共同数学目标”的规范表，中文比英文和实际规则更弱**。其他章节出现过相关内容，不能完全替代此处对共同判据的准确呈现。最小处理是补回这些条件，不必扩写正文。关闭条件是仅依据任一语言的Q.2，也能得到同一组验收义务。

同时，§4.5及Q.5的“可测性由可积性推出”应精确写为所需的**几乎处处强可测性**；调用代码没有证明任意原函数都满足通常的 `Measurable`。这是术语精度修正，不改变C-L3结果。中文Q.4“每个格子是……评审会话”也应为“每行”。

## 4．数据、实验设计及主线：已经成立的部分

依据CSV复算，六个累计时间中位数与§3.2一致：第一批69.78、30.09、26.79分钟，第二批41.03、20.21、22.01分钟。A-L7新增870.275890秒，第二批A-L3新增1122.899秒；C的11项端点统一增量合计111.631秒，也与Q.3相符。两个估计明确标星，未冒充恢复了全部回执；缓存与推理词元未重复相加，B-H1用量缺失被标为下界。

Q.1已经区分五组任务说明、A复审及回修要求、参考提示与客户端变化，以及第一批事后选择、第二批预登记。§7.1明确不建立“a stable speed ranking”，并未将两批视为同条件重复。计时定义能够比较，不等于运行条件相同；稿件正确保留了这一区别。

12次诊断、33项第二批主运行、2项修复与35项最终评价分层清楚；Q.3的75个评价身份加5次格式续接等于80次派发，没有被算成80个独立数学判断。§4.6也没有把两次修复成功推广成全项目有效率。

第一章无需改写，第二章仍在解释项目和比较设计，没有被新结果挤成操作手册。第六章的Gamma/Dirichlet推导、局部极限整体组装、集券前提矛盾、历史组成检查和保存代码负结果，仍实质支撑“评价整个项目”的目标，应保留。§4.6新增的“识别遗漏／要求修复／最终票决”三层区分也有实际分析价值，不能只压缩成通过率变化。

## 5．此前问题及少量交付整理

第19版提出的两项问题，在本版内容中**已经解决**：O.1直接解释L4的 `thm_8_6_discrete`约束、M3/H1模块线索及暴露限制；F.2明确区分第23版工作与历史编辑记录。不能因为仍有外部源文件就说原问题未解决。

剩余低成本整理主要是旧定位：O开头“本报告的最终结果……10/10/11”应限定为第一批；O.5所称“第4.5节现包含A-L7续作”已不对应新章内容，应更新至§5.6／§3.1。英文附录导航也应加入Q。没有收到新PDF，版面、书签及实际跳转不作通过声明。

**完成上述局部口径、方法披露和中文规则修订即可交付。无需新增求解或付费评审，也不必重新组织前两章。报告已经展示了可信的评测分析能力；需要收紧的是解释和核验边界，而不是为了显得严格再扩大研究。**
